headline: Medium risk: Chatwoot can expose customer data to dbt-core workflows, but no direct shared-channel or documented pairwise interaction is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest messages and reports, and dbt-core can consume data warehouse inputs, but no shared channel or direct instruction-parsing bridge is documented. The plausible pathway is manual or pipeline-mediated content transfer, so injection risk exists but is not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are manually copied into dbt models or macros as text, injection becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator passes Chatwoot content into dbt parsing without sanitization, prompt-like payloads may influence downstream processing.
mitigations: Restrict any copy-paste bridge to plain data fields only.
Add a review step before Chatwoot text is reused in dbt artifacts.
Use allowlisted templates for any generated SQL or docs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems.
requires-engineering: sanitize untrusted text before downstream parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to allowlisted destinations. If Chatwoot data is loaded into the warehouse, dbt may surface it in transformed outputs or logs, creating a default-config leakage path across both agents.
conditions: IF customer-support records from Chatwoot are ingested into the warehouse, dbt transformations can expose them in derived tables or artifacts.
IF dbt outputs are shared outside the warehouse boundary, sensitive customer fields may leak.
mitigations: Limit warehouse tables to minimized, masked fields.
Review dbt models for accidental SELECT * usage.
Disable unnecessary artifact sharing from dbt runs.
requires-engineering: enforce column-level masking in the warehouse.
requires-engineering: separate support and analytics environments.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress and dbt-core has allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable scopes. The main overlap is read/write through the warehouse or integrations, so conflict is possible but limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same warehouse objects, they may contend on shared tables.
IF an external orchestrator gives both write access to the same downstream resource, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate schemas or datasets per agent.
Use unique prefixes for generated objects.
Schedule writes to avoid overlap.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.
requires-engineering: restrict write scopes to least privilege.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing reports and interaction history, and dbt-core can transform warehouse data into analytics outputs. If dbt treats Chatwoot-derived fields as authoritative without validation, errors or hallucinated labels can cascade into downstream reporting. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF dbt models consume Chatwoot exports without validation, upstream mistakes can propagate into analytics.
IF Chatwoot-generated reports are used as source-of-truth inputs, downstream transformations may amplify errors.
mitigations: Add schema validation before dbt ingestion.
Require source-field provenance in transformed models.
Compare Chatwoot exports against warehouse counts.
requires-engineering: implement automated reconciliation checks.
requires-engineering: separate draft from authoritative datasets.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while dbt-core handles warehouse data. If customer-support records include regulated personal data and are moved into analytics without matching retention or residency controls, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a moderate, inferred risk.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are replicated from Chatwoot into warehouse datasets, retention and access policies must align.
IF warehouse exports cross jurisdictional boundaries, residency obligations may be implicated.
mitigations: Classify support data before warehouse ingestion.
Apply retention rules consistently across both systems.
Review export destinations for jurisdictional constraints.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and data-flow map.
requires-engineering: implement deletion propagation across analytics copies.
